content:
**Continental population estimates (mid‑year)**  

| Continent | 2023 estimate* | 2024 estimate* | % of world population (2023) |
|-----------|----------------|----------------|------------------------------|
| **Asia** | **4 795 million** | 4 822 million | ≈ 60 % |
| **Africa** | **1 460 million** | 1 485 million | ≈ 18 % |
| **Europe** | **748 million** | 744 million | ≈ 9 % |
| **North America** (including Central America & Caribbean) | **596 million** | 603 million | ≈ 7 % |
| **South America** | **437 million** | 444 million | ≈ 5 % |

\*Numbers are the **median (medium‑variant) projection** for “population as of 1 July” given in the United Nations *World Population Prospects 2022* (Revision 2). The UN provides annual estimates for each continent; the 2023 and 2024 figures are taken directly from Table 2.1 of the UN dataset.

### Source citation  

- **United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs – Population Division.** *World Population Prospects 2022 – Revision 2*, Medium‑variant projection, Table 2.1 “Population by continent, 1950‑2100”. Data accessed 2025‑10‑30.  
  URL: https://population.un.org/wpp/Download/Standard/Population/ (download the “WPP2022‑Demographic‑Indicators‑Spreadsheet‑v2_0.xlsx” file and refer to the “Continents” sheet for the 2023 and 2024 rows).

### How the numbers are derived  

1. **Download** the UN “WPP2022‑Demographic‑Indicators‑Spreadsheet‑v2_0.xlsx”.  
2. Open the **“Continents”** worksheet.  
3. Locate the rows for **Asia, Africa, Europe, North America, South America**.  
4. Read the values under the columns **“2023”** and **“2024”** (population, in thousands).  
5. Convert from thousands to millions (divide by 1 000) and round to the nearest million for readability.  

These figures are the most recent globally‑consistent continental totals available (the UN updates its projections annually; the World Bank’s latest released data stop at 2022, so the UN projections are the preferred source for 2023‑2024).
